value.note: Healing Sanctuary: an ally who begins their turn in this aura gains 10 temporary Hit Points that last 1 round. Rounds are not tracked, so it adds no number here.
Wide Overwatch: your overwatch field is a 60-foot emanation instead of 30 feet.
Aura of Faith: each willing ally in the aura adds the holy trait to their Strikes if you are holy, or the unholy trait if you are unholy.
Aura of Determination: you and all allies in the aura gain a +1 status bonus to saves against mental, morph and polymorph effects.
Aura of Life: you and all allies in the aura gain resistance 5 to void damage and a +1 status bonus to saves against void effects. Your own resistance is permanent and already on your sheet.

Aura of Righteousness: you and all allies in the aura gain resistance 5 to unholy spells, Strikes and other unholy effects, and the aura counteracts teleportation that would move an unholy creature out of it (using your devotion spells’ rank and DC).
Aura of Despair: enemies in the aura take a −1 circumstance penalty to saves against fear, and an enemy that ends its turn inside cannot reduce its frightened value below 1.
Aura of Courage: at the end of your turn, each ally in the aura reduces its frightened value by 1. (Your own reduction is not the aura — it applies wherever you are.)
Divine Health: allies in the aura share your bonus against diseases and poisons, but theirs is +1 rather than +2. They do not share the success-to-critical-success upgrade.

Oath of the Defender: allies in the aura — NOT you — get resistance 2 to damage dealt by creatures of the kind you swore against, rising to 3 at 7th, 4 at 12th and 5 at 17th, and +5 more when such a creature triggers your champion’s reaction.

Wyrmbane Aura: you and all allies within 15 feet gain resistance equal to your Charisma modifier to acid, cold, electricity, fire and poison — half your level instead when the source is a dragon’s breath. Your own resistance is permanent and already on your sheet.
Aura of Preservation: you and all allies within 15 feet gain a +1 status bonus to Fortitude and Will saves against effects from aberrations.
Expand Aura: a single action expands the aura to a 30-foot radius until the start of your next turn — for 1 minute from 10th level, and until you Dismiss it from 16th.

Blessed Swiftness: when an ally’s movement inside the aura triggers an enemy’s reaction, that ally gains a +2 status bonus to all defenses against it. (The +5-foot Speed is yours wherever you stand and is already on your sheet.)

Glorious Banner: the banner now affects a 60-foot emanation (80-foot burst with Plant Banner), the allies’ fear bonus rises to +2, you and affected allies gain +1 status to AC, Fortitude and Reflex saves, and enemies inside that can see the banner take a −2 status penalty to Will saves.
Battle-Tested Companion: while the banner is affixed to that companion the aura is 10 feet larger than normal — typically 40 feet instead of 30.
Channel Your Divine Spark: the nimbus activates if it was off and its area doubles — bright light for 60 feet, dim for 60 more — and you cannot suppress it while channeling.

Aura Shaping: you choose the emanation’s size, any multiple of 5 from 5 feet up to 20 feet, when you Channel Elements or use a stance impulse that affects it. The maximum rises by 5 feet at 15th and 20th levels.

Adept Benefit (7th): the +1 status bonus now applies to ALL saves against mental effects rather than only fear, and you and allies in the aura gain a +2 status bonus to damage rolls (+3 at 11th, +4 at 17th).

Paragon Benefit (17th): allies in the aura are not off-guard from being flanked unless you are flanked too, and an ally in the aura that is clumsy, enfeebled, frightened, sickened or stupefied takes a status penalty 1 lower than the condition value — unless you have the same condition.

value:
A blade of shearing wind races away from you in a 60-foot line. Each creature in the area takes 2d4 slashing damage with a basic Reflex save against your class DC. In the final square of the line, the boomerang whirls in place until the end of your next turn. Any creature that ends its turn in that square has to save against the boomerang.

On your next turn, you can use a single action, which has the concentrate trait, to return the boomerang to you. It returns in a line from its square to your current location, with the same effect as the initial line, then the impulse ends. You must have line of effect to the boomerang and be within 60 feet of it.

---

**Level (+2)** The damage increases by 1d4.

Tapping into the physiology of your draconic ancestor, you can exhale a torrent of energy in a 15-foot cone or a 30-foot line, dealing 1d4 damage. Each creature in the area must attempt a basic saving throw against the higher of your class DC or spell DC. You can't use this ability again for 1d4 rounds.

At 3rd level and every 2 levels thereafter, the damage increases by 1d4. The shape of the breath, the damage type, and the saving throw match those of your draconic exemplar. This ability has the trait associated with the type of damage it deals.

**Requirements** You're holding or wearing a healer's toolkit.

---

You can patch up wounds, even in combat. Attempt a Medicine check with the same DC as for Treat Wounds and restore the corresponding amount of HP; this doesn't remove the wounded condition. As with Treat Wounds, you can attempt checks against higher DCs if you have the minimum proficiency rank. The target is then immune to your Battle Medicine for 1 day. This does not make them immune to, or otherwise count as, Treat Wounds.

**Requirements** You're wearing or holding a Healer's Toolkit.

---

You spend 10 minutes treating one injured living creature (targeting yourself, if you so choose). The target is then temporarily immune to Treat Wounds actions for 1 hour, but this interval overlaps with the time you spent treating (so a patient can be treated once per hour, not once per 70 minutes).

The Medicine check DC is usually 15, though the GM might adjust it based on the circumstances, such as treating a patient outside in a storm, or treating magically cursed wounds. If you're an expert in Medicine, you can instead attempt a DC 20 check to increase the Hit Points regained by 10; if you're a master of Medicine, you can instead attempt a DC 30 check to increase the Hit Points regained by 30; and if you're legendary, you can instead attempt a DC 40 check to increase the Hit Points regained by 50. The damage dealt on a critical failure remains the same.

If you succeed at your check, you can continue treating the target to grant additional healing. If you treat it for a total of 1 hour, double the Hit Points it regains from Treat Wounds.

The result of your Medicine check determines how many Hit Points the target regains.

Treat Wounds

---

**Critical Success** The target regains 4d8 Hit Points and loses the wounded condition.

**Success** The target regains 2d8 Hit Points, and loses the wounded condition.

**Critical Failure** The target takes 1d8 damage.

Resonance

Source Rage of Elements pg. 43

Ability Type Specific Familiar - Elemental Wisp

30 feet. Your wisp vibrates at a frequency attuned to their element, resonating with and empowering all effects sharing that trait. Creatures in the area gain a +1 status bonus to damage rolls for alchemical and magical effects with the same elemental trait as your wisp. If your wisp is a wood wisp, the status bonus also applies to damage rolls for effects with the plant trait.

Elemental Diplomat

Source Rage of Elements pg. 43

Ability Type Specific Familiar - Gennayn

A gennayn's modifier for Diplomacy is equal to your level plus your key spellcasting attribute modifier, rather than just your level. The gennayn gets a +1 circumstance bonus to Diplomacy checks against elementals and grants you the same bonus if you're in the same space.

Scamp Elements

Source Rage of Elements pg. 43

Ability Type Specific Familiar - Elemental Scamp

An elemental scamp's element or elements are set. You choose a type of scamp and can't change the element each day. This determines the scamp's elemental traits and the damage type of their Elemental Breath. Air (air) slashing damage; earth (earth) bludgeoning damage; fire (fire) fire damage; metal (metal) slashing damage; water (water) acid damage; wood (plant, wood) poison damage.

Elemental Mobility

Source Rage of Elements pg. 43

Ability Type Specific Familiar - Gennayn

Your gennayn gains a familiar ability depending on its element. Air gennayns gain flier, earth gennayns gain burrower, fire gennayns gain jet, metal gennayns gain levitator, water gennayns gain amphibious, and wood gennayns gain climber.

Sorcerous Sweets

Source Wake the Dead #3 pg. 25

Ability Type Specific Familiar - Sweet Beasts (Chocolate Mouse)

During your daily preparations, your sweetened familiar conducts an unusual little ritual. Your familiar find a small non-magical object (a flower or piece of fallen fruit by preference, but a pebble or even a coin will do in a pinch) and then does a curious ritual dance around—gingerbread sparrows hop and chirp, while hard candy beetles turndle in increasingly complex geometric patterns and chocolate mice make arcane sigils with their paws. At the rite's conclusion, the object turns into a piece of candy, usually of the same sort as the familiar. The candy is an item with the arcane, consumable and transmutation traits. Anyone who eats the candy as an Interact action gains a +1 item bonus to Deception, Diplomacy, and Performance checks for 1 hour (this increases to +2 at level 9, and +3 at level 17). The candy maintains its enchantment until your next daily preparations.

Extra Reagents

Source Core Rulebook pg. 218

Ability Type Master

Your familiar grows extra infused reagents on or in its body. You gain an additional batch of infused reagents. You must have the infused reagents ability to select this ability.

Aeon Stone Reservoir

Source Player Core 2 pg. 170

Ability Type Specific Familiar - Aeon Wyrd

Your aeon wyrd can house any aeon stone as a powerfully resonant nucleus that holds it together. You gain the aeon stone’s benefits without needing to invest it, and you gain the aeon stone’s resonant power. This doesn’t interfere with any wayfinder you invest.

Can't Walk

Source Player Core 2 pg. 170

Ability Type Specific Familiar - Aeon Wyrd

Your aeon wyrd has no land Speed.

Crystalline

Source Player Core 2 pg. 170

Ability Type Specific Familiar - Aeon Wyrd

Your aeon wyrd's crystalline structure makes it vulnerable to sonic attacks. It gains weakness to sonic equal to your level.

Porter

Source Player Core 2 pg. 171

Ability Type Specific Familiar - Homunculus

You can choose for your homunculus to have either item delivery or valet.

Blood Link

Source Player Core 2 pg. 171

Ability Type Specific Familiar - Homunculus

(mental) A homunculus is telepathically linked to its creator using their shared blood as a conduit, allowing it to share information back and forth at a range of 1,500 feet, including its master’s knowledge and everything the homunculus hears. If you become unconscious and dying, your homunculus senses the waning power in your blood, allowing it to automatically act on the next turn as if you Commanded it. If the homunculus is destroyed, the master takes 2d10 mental damage.

Imp Invisibility

Source Player Core 2 pg. 171

Ability Type Specific Familiar - Imp

Once per hour, your imp familiar can cast invisibility on itself as a divine innate spell.

Scholarly Linguist

Source Player Core 2 pg. 171

Ability Type Specific Familiar - Pipefox

Thanks to its innate erudition, your pipefox speaks and understands all languages you know (instead of just one) as well as one common language you don’t know.

Flammable

Source Player Core 2 pg. 171

Ability Type Specific Familiar - Poppet

Your poppet’s components make it particularly vulnerable to fire. It gains weakness to fire equal to your level. You can use one familiar ability to reinforce the poppet’s construction, removing this weakness for the day.

Magic Scent

Source Player Core 2 pg. 171

Ability Type Specific Familiar - Spellslime

Your spellslime familiar gains an imprecise sense with a range of 30 feet that enables it to smell magic of the same tradition as your own.

Ooze Defense

Source Player Core 2 pg. 171

Ability Type Specific Familiar - Spellslime

Your spellslime familiar is easy to hit, but it lacks weak points. It is immune to critical hits and precision damage, but its AC is only 10 + your level (instead of an AC equal to yours).

Slime Rejuvenation

Source Player Core 2 pg. 171

Ability Type Specific Familiar - Spellslime

Your spellslime familiar gains the focused rejuvenation ability, but it recovers 2 Hit Points per level when you Refocus instead of 1.

Stylus Claws

Source Rival Academies pg. 46

Ability Type Specific Familiar - Calligraphy Wyrm

The wyrm has stylus-shaped claws that it can fill with its natural ink, using its claw as a pen without having to purchase ink.

Bound to Mortal

Source Gatewalkers (Hardcover) pg. 241

Ability Type Specific Familiar - Spirit Guide

Your familiar gains unique benefits from its bond to you. Your familiar gains an additional 10 Hit Points and can make an either a jaws or claws unarmed attack using your normal melee attack bonus. You choose whether it has a jaws or claws unarmed attack when you first gain the spirit guide as your familiar. If it has a jaws unarmed attack, the attack deals 1d6 piercing damage and is in the brawling group. If you choose the claws unarmed attack, it deals 1d4 slashing damage, has the agile trait, and is in the brawling group.

Gold Scent

Source High Seas pg. 51

Ability Type Specific Familiar - Golden Ermine

Your golden stoat familiar gains an imprecise sense with a range of 30 feet that enables it to smell objects made of gold.

Fruity Ambrosia

Source High Seas pg. 51

Ability Type Specific Familiar - Wildtwig

The peach growing from a wildtwig’s horn is magical, tasting like the favorite fruit of the one who consumes it, providing them some temporary rejuvenation. A single fruit lasts for 8 hours after picked. When consumed as an Interact action, the peach provides temporary Hit Points equal to the creature’s level for 1 hour. Eating a second fruit within an hour provides no benefits, instead making the creature sickened 1 for 10 minutes. It takes 10 minutes for the wildtwig to grown another, and during this time, they must remain calm and focused on producing the fruit; they are unable to perform any other actions.

Constructed

Source PFS Guide pg. 122

Ability Type Specific Familiar - Aeon Wyrd

Your aeon wyrd is immune to bleed, death effects, disease, doomed, drained, fatigued, healing, necromancy, nonlethal attacks, paralyzed, poison, sickened, and unconscious. It can recover Hit Points only via the Repair action and other methods that fix items, not from any form of Hit Point healing. It's destroyed at 0 HP.

Detect Magic

Source PFS Guide pg. 123

Ability Type Specific Familiar - Dweomercat Cub

Your dweomercat cub can cast 1st-level detect magic as an arcane innate spell.

Slink In Shadows

Source Secrets of Magic pg. 229

Ability Type Specific Familiar - Shadow Familiar

The shadow familiar can Hide or end its Sneak in a creature's or object's shadow.

Clockwork

Source Grand Bazaar pg. 23

Ability Type Specific Familiar - Clockwork Familiar

You need to keep your clockwork familiar wound, but the process isn't particularly onerous or time consuming. If you spend 1 minute winding up your clockwork familiar with a unique key only you can use, it can remain active for 24 hours, after which time it becomes unaware of its surroundings and can't act until it's wound again.

 Enemies can attempt to disable the clockwork familiar, with a standard DC for your level to Disable a Device, to reduce the remaining operational time by 1 hour (or 2 hours on a critical success). Certain other abilities that adversely affect technology might also reduce the clockwork familiar's remaining operational time.

 Some abilities, like Steam Screen, require your clockwork familiar to spend some of its remaining operational time. It can't spend more than it has and shuts down immediately once it has no time remaining.

 You can wind your clockwork familiar for 1 minute at any time to return it to the maximum 24 hours of operational time.

Electricity Vulnerability

Source Grand Bazaar pg. 23

Ability Type Specific Familiar - Clockwork Familiar

The metal components of a clockwork familiar conduct electricity and are easily disrupted by an electric current. It gains weakness to electricity damage equal to your level.

Nosoi Resistance

Source Grand Bazaar pg. 35

Ability Type Specific Familiar - Nosoi

A nosoi has resistance to negative and poison damage equal to half your level.

Divinatory Linguist

Source Grand Bazaar pg. 35

Ability Type Specific Familiar - Pipefox

Thanks to its innate tendency for divinations, your pipefox speaks and understands all languages you know (instead of just one) as well as one common language you don't know.

Lend a Hand

Source Book of the Dead pg. 40

Ability Type Specific Familiar - Crawling Hand

The crawling hand assists an ally in the same space to attack a foe, crawling over the enemy and grabbing to distract them. Despite being a minion, it gains 1 reaction at the start of its turns, which it can use only to Aid an attack roll by an ally that shares the hand's space (it still has to prepare to help as normal for the Aid reaction). This attempt automatically succeeds. If the crawling hand has a similar ability, like partner in crime, it still gains only 1 reaction and can choose how to spend it.

Undead

Source Book of the Dead pg. 40

Ability Type Specific Familiar - Crawling Hand

Your familiar is undead. It has negative healing and is immune to death effects, disease, poison, and unconscious. It's destroyed at 0 HP.

Invisibility

Source Book of the Dead pg. 40

Ability Type Specific Familiar - Old Friend

Once per hour, your familiar can cast 2nd-level invisibility on itself as a divine innate spell.

Anchored Incorporeality

Source Book of the Dead pg. 40

Ability Type Specific Familiar - Old Friend

While most ghosts are bound to the site where they died or were buried, some instead find themselves bound to specific items, such as a particular piece of jewelry, article of clothing, pet's collar, or a stone from a building in which it dwelled. These items, known as anchors, were important to the ghost in life, or critical to the events of their death and haunting.

 A creature with anchored incorporeality has the incorporeal trait, meaning it can move through physical creatures and such creatures can move through it. It can't attempt Strength-based checks (such as Grapple) against corporeal creatures and corporeal creatures can't attempt such checks against it. Though incorporeal, a creature with anchored incorporeality can travel no more than 60 feet from its anchor and must maintain line of effect to the anchor. This typically prevents it from moving through walls. Unlike many other incorporeal creatures, a creature with anchored incorporeality doesn't have resistance to all damage or immunity to precision damage.

 A character with an animal companion or familiar that has anchored incorporeality can transfer the anchor to a new item with a special ritual. This requires spending 1 week in concert with the companion to create a new anchor. A character who knows this technique might be able to adapt it to transfer a ghost's Site Bound ability (or similar restriction) to tie it to an anchor instead of a place.

Heads Will Roll

Source Book of the Dead pg. 40

Ability Type Specific Familiar - Talking Head

Unless its master gives the talking head the flier ability, a talking head is able to move only by rolling along the ground, reducing its speed to 15 feet. Alternatively, a creature can, as a single action, kick or throw the head 30 feet. This can't be used as an attack; the head bounces harmlessly off anything it hits.

Tenacious Mind

Source Shadows at Sundown pg. 53

Ability Type Specific Familiar - House Drake

Once per day, as long as your house drake took no actions on the previous round, you gain the following.
Ferocious Will (reaction) (abjuration, arcane, mental) Trigger You succeed at a saving throw against a magical mental effect; Effect You send a blast of magical feedback at the effect's source, dealing 2d6 mental damage (basic Will save against your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher) to that creature. On a failed save, the creature is also slowed 1 for 1 round.

Created Magic

Source Impossible Lands pg. 220

Ability Type Specific Familiar - Ceru

Your ceru familiar grants you the mage hand and guidance cantrips via the cantrip connection granted ability. If one or more of these cantrips isn't on your spell list, you can replace the cantrip or cantrips not on your spell list with a cantrip or cantrips from your spell list instead.

Crystal Scent

Source Rage of Elements pg. 42

Ability Type Specific Familiar - Cullitox Shardling

A cullitox can sense crystals or gems within 60 feet as if using the scent ability.

Innate Element

Source Rage of Elements pg. 43

Ability Type Specific Familiar - Elemental Wisp

An elemental wisp's element is set. You choose the element when you gain the specific familiar and can't change it each day.

Polong

Source Book of the Dead pg. 40

Required Number of Abilities 8

Granted Abilities Flier, Lifelink, Skilled (Society), Speech, Spellcasting

Polongs are wicked, invisible spirits created from the blood of murder victims, bound to glass bottles, and fed with the blood of their master. They're often used to possess and sicken their master's enemies. Polongs can't be found or acquired, only created, a process that can take up to two weeks. If a polong's bottle is ever destroyed, or if its master fails to provide its daily feeding of blood, the polong withers and dies.

options.label: Homing Drake (acid)
options.note: A 30-foot line of caustic spittle dealing 1d4 acid damage with a basic Reflex save against your Dragonet Breath DC.

options.label: House Drake (arcane, mental)
options.note: A 15-foot cone of silver mist dealing 1d4 mental damage with a basic Will save against your Dragonet Breath DC. It counts as silver for the purpose of weaknesses.

options.label: Pearl Dragonet (arcane, curse)
options.note: A 15-foot cone of golden mist. Each use, decide whether it gives good luck or bad luck; an affected creature is then temporarily immune for 1 hour. Good luck: each creature in the area gains a +1 status bonus to its next attack roll or skill check before the start of your next turn. Bad luck: each creature attempts a Will save against your Dragonet Breath DC, and on a failure takes a –1 status penalty to that next roll; on a critical failure it instead rolls twice and takes the worse result (a misfortune effect). No damage.

options.label: Tidepool Dragonet (fire)
options.note: A 15-foot line of superheated gas dealing 1d4 fire damage with a basic Reflex save against your Dragonet Breath DC. You can use it underwater despite the fire trait; if you do, it gains the water trait and emerges as a 20-foot cone of boiling water instead.

value: Damage rises by 1d4 at 3rd level and every 2 levels after — 2d4 at 3rd, 3d4 at 5th, up to 10d4 at 19th — on the three heritages that deal damage. After you use Dragonet Breath you can’t use it again for 1d4 rounds. The activity gains the traits listed in parentheses for your heritage.

Any bonuses, runes and magical abilities of your actual armor are suppressed while it is worn, and any that could apply to the carapace are replicated onto it. At 4th level and every 3 levels after (the impulse’s Level +3 entry), its Hardness increases by 1, its HP by 4 and its BT by 2.

value.name: Grim Fascination: Blood
value.description:
Blood necromancers, also known as sanguimancers, manipulate their own blood and the flowing blood of their enemies. Your thralls often resemble vampiric spawn or constructs of hardened blood.

**Grave Spell** Blood Infusion

**Thrall Enhancement** Your thralls are enhanced with a drop of your blood, and when they fall, your blood returns to you. Whenever a thrall is destroyed, you regain 1 Hit Point. At 5th level and every 4 levels thereafter, the amount of Hit Points you regain when a thrall is destroyed increases by 1.

value.name: Grim Fascination: Bone
value.description:
Bone necromancers, also known as osteomancers, craft what they desire from the skeletons of the dead or simply create new skeletons by expanding and shaping small bone pieces.

**Grave Spell** Bone Spear

**Thrall Enhancement** Your thralls are well constructed and nimble. Each of your thralls' Speed is increased by 5 feet.

value.name: Grim Fascination: Flesh
value.description:
Flesh necromancers, also known as caromancers, are experts at the destruction, production, and manipulation of flesh and muscles. Your thralls generally take on the form of zombies and other creatures of dead flesh.

**Grave Spell** Dead Weight

**Thrall Enhancement** You can still make use of a destroyed thrall's flesh. Whenever one of your thralls is destroyed, you can cause the thrall to leave behind difficult terrain in the space it was destroyed. The difficult terrain lasts 10 minutes.

value.name: Grim Fascination: Spirit
value.description:
Spirit necromancers, also known as vitamancers, seek the secrets of the soul and play with the eternal energies of the living and dead. Your thralls often resemble ghosts and spirits.

**Grave Spell** Life Tap

**Thrall Enhancement** Your thralls, while still being tied to the physical world, have an incorporeal essence. Whenever one of your thralls Strikes, you can choose for that damage to be spirit or void damage instead of physical damage.

value: A resonant weapon channels the energy of the plane it is attuned to. You gain the Conduct Energy free action while wielding a resonant weapon.

value.name: Consume Thrall
value.requirements: You have 0 Focus Points and at least one thrall within 30 feet of you.
value.description: You destroy one thrall within 30 feet of you and regain 1 Focus Point. You can spend this Focus Point only to cast a grave spell.

value.name: Puppeteer
value.description:
You prefer to study life and death from afar. You gain the Consume Thrall action and the thrall proliferation ability.

**Thrall Proliferation** Once per round when you cast *create thrall*, you can create one additional thrall in range.

value.name: Reaper
value.description:
You study flesh up close by clashing blade against bone. You gain the reaper's edge and thrall teamwork abilities.

**Reaper's Edge** You become trained in martial weapons and medium armor. At 11th level, you become an expert in martial weapons, and at 13th you become an expert in medium armor.

**Thrall Teamwork** Once per round after you cast *create thrall*, you can make a melee Strike as a free action against a creature within your melee reach that is adjacent to at least one of your thralls.

value.name: Atryl, Rune of Fire
value.usage: drawn on a crature or object
value.description:
This rune is often placed on a stone in a hearth, its power ensuring the stone remains warm through the night. The bearer’s fire resistance, if any, is reduced by 5. Its immunities are unaffected.

Invocation
The bearer takes 1d8 fire damage with a basic Fortitude save. On a critical failure, it's also dazzled for 1 round.

Level (+2) The reduction in fire resistance increases by 1, and the damage of the invocation increases by 1d8.

value.name: Baruiel, Rune of Hold's Bravery
value.description:
This scratched rune reminds the bearer to stand strong against fear when near allies. As long as the rune-bearer is within 10 feet of one of its allies, whenever it would reduce its frightened condition by 1, it instead reduces it by 2.

Invocation
The essence of the rune is released outward, easing the minds of others. Each ally of the rune-bearer within a 10-foot emanation reduces their frightened condition by 2.

value.name: Camonica, Rune of Perplexity
value.description:
This rune of looping swirls is difficult to look straight at and stirs up a psychic cacophony in a foe's mind. The first time each round the rune-bearer takes an action with the concentrate trait, the turmoil increases, dealing it 2 mental damage.

Invocation
The cacophony fragments and expands rapidly in a mental explosion, dealing 1d4 mental damage to the rune- bearer with a basic Will save. On a failure, the rune-bearer is stupefied 1 for 1 round (or stupefied 2 on a critical failure).

Level (+2) The damage from the mental turmoil increases by 1 and the damage of the invocation increases by 1d4.

value.name: Esvadir, Rune of Whetstones
value.usage: drawn on a weapon or unarmed attack that deals piercing or slashing damage
value.description:
This cuspate rune, when placed on a blade, ensures it won't go dull. Strikes with the weapon or unarmed attack deal an extra 2 persistent bleed damage per weapon damage die.

Invocation
A blast of cutting energy is released outward from the rune, dealing 1d8 slashing damage to a creature adjacent to the rune-bearer, with a basic Reflex save.

Level (+2) The damage of the invocation increases by 1d8.

value.name: Holtrik, Rune of Dwarven Ramparts
value.description:
Similarity in the Dwarven words for “wall” and “shield” ensure that this angular rune, once used to shore up tunnels, can apply equally well in the heat of battle. A creature that has the shield raised gains a +1 status bonus to AC.

Invocation
You call the shield to its rightful place. You Raise the Shield bearing the rune, as if the rune-bearer had used Raise a Shield, and the shield's status bonus to AC lasts until the beginning of the creature's next turn.

value.name: Ledria, Rune of Appeal
value.description:
No matter what skin, shell, or scale this rune is drawn on, it shines like gold. The rune-bearer gains a +1 status bonus to Deception, Diplomacy, and Performance checks.

Invocation
The rune draws creatures closer to the bearer. Each creature within 30 feet of the rune-bearer can Step closer to the rune-bearer as a free action.

Level (9th) The bonus increases to +2.

Level (17th) The bonus increases to +3.

value.name: Lyskel, Rune of Frost
value.usage: drawn on a creature or object
value.description:
This rune is often placed on chests and boxes to keep their contents from spoiling, even in the hottest of climates. The rune-bearer takes a –5-foot circumstance penalty to its Speeds and becomes so cold that movement becomes dangerous; if the bearer takes a move action, it becomes clumsy 1 until the beginning of its next turn.

Invocation
The rune-bearer takes 1d4 cold damage, with a basic Fortitude save. All squares on the ground in the bearer's space and adjacent squares are covered in snow, becoming difficult terrain for 1 round.

Level (+2) The damage of the invocation increases by 1d4.

value.name: Marssyl, Rune of Impact
value.usage: drawn on a weapon or unarmed attack that deals bludgeoning damage
value.description:
This rune magnifies force many times over as it passes through the rune's concentric rings. The weapon or unarmed attack deals 1 bludgeoning splash damage per weapon damage die. If the rune is on a melee weapon or melee unarmed attack, you and the rune-bearer are immune to this splash damage.

Invocation
The rune vibrates as power concentrates within it. The next successful Strike made with the weapon or unarmed attack before the end of its wielder's next turn deals an additional die of damage, and the target must succeed at a Fortitude save against your class DC or be pushed 10 feet away from the attacker (20 feet on a critical failure).

value.name: Oljinex, Rune of Cowards' Bane
value.description:
This rune resembles a broken arrow. The shield bearing the rune gains a +2 status bonus to its Hardness against physical damage from ranged attacks.

Invocation
(illusion, mental, visual) The rune creates an illusion in the minds of all creatures adjacent to the rune-bearer that lasts for 1 round. The illusion is of a large, impassable wall blocking all paths away from the rune-bearer. Creatures affected by this invocation can't willingly move farther away from the rune-bearer for 1 round or until they disbelieve the illusion, usually by using a Seek action.

Level (+4) The status bonus to Hardness increases by 1.

value.name: Pluuna, Rune of Illumination
value.usage: drawn on a creature or armor
value.description:
While many runes emit a faint glow, illumination is the focus of this simple rune. The rune sheds bright light in a 20-foot emanation (and dim light to 40 feet). Creatures in the emanation take a –1 item penalty to Stealth checks.

Invocation
Each creature in the light must succeed at a Fortitude save against your class DC or be dazzled for 1 round. The light fades, but the target still sheds dim light in a 20-foot emanation for 1 round.

value.name: Ranshu, Rune of Thunder
value.usage: drawn on a creature or object
value.description:
This vertical rune is often carved on tall towers to draw lightning and shield the buildings below it. If the rune-bearer doesn't take a move action at least once on its turn, a small bolt of static finds it, dealing 3 electricity damage.

Invocation
The preliminary streaks of lightning braid together into a powerful bolt. The rune-bearer takes 1d8 electricity damage with a basic Fortitude save.

Level (+2) The damage from the bolt of static increases by 1, and the damage of the invocation increases by 1d8.

value.name: Rehgog, Rune of Bestial Might
value.description:
The jagged edges of this rune evoke the claws and talons of mighty beasts. The target's nose becomes an animal-like snout, giving the rune-bearer scent as an imprecise scent with a range of 30 feet.

Invocation
The rune-bearer's muscles bulge with the strength of a ferocious beast. The bearer can immediately Step as a free action. The next unarmed Strike the bearer attempts before the start of your next turn deals an additional die of damage.

value.name: Sertum, Rune of Preparedness
value.description:
The wavy lines of this rune evoke fields of reeds, the branches of trees blowing in the wind, or other natural phenomena. The rune-bearer gains a +1 status bonus to Survival checks and to Lore checks related to a type of terrain or specific natural location you choose as you draw the rune. The rune-bearer can use Survival to roll initiative, and the status bonus applies to this roll.

Invocation
The rune reaches out to the surrounding terrain, shifting it to the rune-bearer's advantage. The rune-bearer can Step up to three times as a free action.

Level (9th) The bonus increases to +2.

Level (17th) The bonus increases to +3.

value.name: Thullax, Rune of Corrosion
value.usage: drawn on a creature or object
value.description:
The swooping lines of this rune seem to melt into each other as if their edges were hazy and indistinct, though the meaning is clear to you. The rune-bearer's resistance to each physical damage type is reduced by 1 (if it has any such resistances). Its immunities are unaffected.

Invocation
The bearer takes 1d6 acid damage with a basic Fortitude save; on a critical failure, it takes 1 persistent acid damage.

Level (+2) The reduction in physical resistance increases by 1, the damage of the invocation increases by 1d6, and the persistent damage increases by 1.

value.name: Tilus, Rune of Vocabulary
value.description:
Upon close inspection, this rune comprises hundreds of smaller characters of various runic languages. When you etch or trace this rune, choose one language you know. The rune-bearer can speak and understand the chosen language and gains a +1 status bonus to Society checks and to Lore checks related to writing (such as Library Lore and Scribing Lore).

Invocation
The rune-bearer's voice rings clear and true, allowing them to automatically succeed at any flat check that could disrupt an auditory action (such as the one imposed by the deafened condition) for 1 round. During this time, the bearer can also speak their true mind even if they are currently confused, controlled, or otherwise unable to speak.

Level (9th) The bonus increases to +2.

Level (17th) The bonus increases to +3.

value.name: Zohk, Rune of Homecoming
value.description:
This circular mark allows travelers to always find their way home. The rune-bearer gains a +15-foot status bonus to its Speeds, but only when its movement would end closer to you than where the creature started its turn.

Invocation
(teleportation) You call the rune-bearer to your side. You teleport the target to any unoccupied square adjacent to you. If the bearer is unwilling, it must succeed at a Will save to negate the effect.

value.name: Av-, Diacritic Rune of Succession
value.description:
This diacritic surrounds the base rune with similar-looking smaller runes to give the impression of distant echoes. When the base rune is invoked, you can Invoke a single Rune on a different rune-bearer within 15 feet of the original rune-bearer as a free action.

You can have only one copy of av-, diacritic rune of succession applied at a given time, and once you invoke it, you can't etch or trace it again for 10 minutes.

value.name: En-, Diacritic Rune of Expansion
value.usage: drawn on a rune that deals damage
value.description: This diacritic surrounds a rune with outward-facing arrows to magnify and direct power outward. When the base rune is invoked, the rune-bearer is affected by it as usual, and each other creature in a 15-foot emanation around the rune-bearer also takes the damage and other effects from the base rune (and can attempt a saving throw if possible). An individual creature can be affected by the rune only once, even if the rune could normally affect more creatures than just the rune-bearer.

value.name: Fob-, Diacritic Rune of Doubling
value.usage: drawn on a rune that doesn't deal damage
value.description: This diacritic consists of pairs of diamonds in opposite positions around the base rune. When the base rune is invoked, the rune-bearer is affected by it as usual, and you can choose to also be affected by the invocation if possible.

value.name: Kit-, Diacritic Rune of Mercy
value.usage: drawn on a rune that deals damage and doesn't have the death or void trait
value.description: This diacritic frames a rune with soft curves that mitigate its deadlier effects but make them harder to resist. When the base rune is invoked, it has the nonlethal trait, but the rune-bearer takes a –1 status penalty to any saving throw.

value.name: Per-, Diacritic Rune of Continuum
value.description:
This whirling diacritic recirculates the magic of the base rune onto another creature. After the base rune is invoked, it automatically traces itself on a different target of your choice within 15 feet of the original rune-bearer.

You can have only one copy of per-, diacritic rune of continuum applied at a given time, and once you invoke it, you can't etch or trace it again for 10 minutes.

value.name: Sun-, Diacritic Rune of Preservation
value.description:
This spiraling diacritic channels the magic of a rune outwards, then back to the same location, allowing a rune to reconstitute itself. After the base rune is invoked, the base rune automatically traces itself back upon the same target.

You can have only one copy of sun-, diacritic rune of preservation applied at a given time, and once you invoke it, you can't Etch or Trace the Rune again for 10 minutes.

value.name: Ti-, Diacritic Rune of Fundaments
value.usage: drawn on a rune that deals acid, cold, electricity, or fire damage
value.description: This wavering diacritic encompasses the base rune to slightly change its meaning. When the base rune is invoked, you can alter the damage its invocation deals, choosing acid, cold, electricity, or fire.

value.name: Ur-, Diacritic Rune of Intensity
value.usage: drawn on a rune that deals damage
value.description: This diacritic accentuates the base rune with bolder lines to give greater weight to its effects. When the base rune is invoked, its invocation gains a status bonus to damage equal to 2 plus half your level.

value.name: Astillu, Rune of Submersion
value.description:
Originating from Thalassic script, this wavy rune is popular with iruxi practitioners of rune magic who want to easily traverse their watery environs. The rune-bearer can breathe underwater and gains a swim Speed equal to its land Speed or 30 feet, whichever is greater. Its melee Strikes don't take the usual circumstance penalty for passing through water.

Invocation
The rune's power pushes the bearer forward in a surprising surge of speed. The rune-bearer can Swim up to 60 feet as a free action, and this movement doesn't trigger reactions.

value.name: Cruonign, Rune of Leeching
value.usage: drawn on a slashing or piercing weapon
value.description:
The jagged shape of this rune resembles a vampire's fangs. Strikes with the rune-bearing weapon deal an additional 3 void damage. Whenever a living creature is damaged by one of these Strikes, the rune-bearer gains temporary Hit Points equal to the void damage the target took (after applying resistances and the like). These temporary Hit Points last 1 round.

Invocation
The rune lashes out in a 30-foot cone from the wielder of the weapon, dealing 4d10 void damage to each creature in the area, with a basic Fortitude save. If any creatures take damage, the wielder regains 12 Hit Points.

Level (+2) The additional void damage increases by 1, the damage of the invocation increases by 1d10, and the healing increases by 3.

value.name: Feikris, Rune of Gravity
value.usage: drawn on a creature wearing armor
value.description:
The lines of this rune overlap strangely, making it seem larger than it really is. The rune-bearer gains a +2 status bonus to Athletics checks. They can Disarm, Grapple, Reposition, Shove, or Trip creatures up to two sizes larger than themself, or three sizes larger if the rune-bearer is legendary in Athletics.

Invocation
All creatures in a 15-foot emanation around the rune-bearer must succeed at a Fortitude save or be pulled 5 feet toward the rune-bearer (or 10 feet on a critical failure).

Level (17th) The status bonus increases to +3.

value.name: Germantria, Rune of Partnership
value.description:
When drawn, this knobby rune pulses with your own heartbeat, creating a vital connection between you and the bearer. While you are within 1 mile of the rune-bearer, it takes half damage from all effects that deal Hit Point damage, and you take the remainder of the damage. When you take this damage, you don't apply any resistances, weaknesses, or other abilities you have to that damage; you simply take that amount of damage. If either you or the rune-bearer is reduced to 0 Hit Points, the rune fades without being invoked.

Invocation
(healing) The connection between you and the rune-bearer is severed in a burst of healing energy. Both you and the rune-bearer regain 20 Hit Points.

Level (+2) The amount of Hit Points healed by the invocation increases by 5.

value.name: Ichelsu, Rune of Observation
value.description:
A ring of dotted circles, this rune allows a creature marked with it to see all. The target is affected by see the unseen and gains all-around vision, which prevents it from being flanked.

Invocation
The eyes of the rune fly outwards, attaching to all creatures in a 20-foot emanation. A creature with an eye attached to it that would be invisible is concealed instead, and one that would be concealed for any other reason is not concealed. This effect lasts for 2 rounds.

value.name: Jurroz, Rune of Dragon Fury
value.description:
This craggy rune channels the fury of dragon kind. Whenever an enemy Strikes or Steals from the rune-bearer, they become off-guard for 1 round.

Invocation
As a free action, the rune-bearer can Fly up to 60 feet toward an enemy that has damaged it or stolen from it in the last minute. If it ends this movement adjacent to the enemy, the enemy becomes off-guard until the end of the rune-bearer's next turn. If the rune-bearer doesn't have a fly Speed and ends its movement in the air, it safely floats back to the ground at the end of its next turn.

value.name: Kojastri, Rune of Insulation
value.description:
This rune insulates from harmful energy of all kinds. The creature wearing the armor gains resistance 4 to your choice of cold, electricity, or fire, and any creature that touches the rune-bearer or damages it with an unarmed attack or non-reach melee weapon takes 2 damage of the chosen type. The rune has the trait of the energy type chosen.

Invocation
Any creature that has the armor's wearer engulfed, grabbed, restrained, or swallowed whole takes 8d4 damage of the rune's chosen type with a basic Reflex save against your class DC. On a failure, it also releases the armor's wearer.

Level (+2) The resistance and damage granted by insulation both increase by 1, and the damage dealt by the invocation increases by 2d4.

value.name: Oraloq, Rune of Inarticulateness
value.description:
This hard-to-read rune makes language difficult for the unfortunate rune-bearer. When the rune-bearer attempts a skill check or ability with the linguistic trait or attempts to Cast a Spell that doesn't have the subtle trait, they must succeed a DC 5 flat check, or the action is lost.

Invocation
The rune-bearer must attempt a Will save as the rune puts a strong mental block on the part of their mind that interprets language. If the rune-bearer fails their save, they take 20 mental damage (or double damage on a critical failure) the first time they use any language, take a linguistic action, or Cast a Spell without the subtle trait. The rune-bearer is aware of this and knows what will trigger the damage. The effect ends once the damage is taken or at the end of the rune-bearer's next turn, whichever comes first.

Level (+2) The damage of the invocation increases by 5.

value.name: Piteregrin, Rune of Transposition
value.description:
The slanted lines and odd curls of this rune give the impression that it is trying to escape. The rune-bearer can use a single action to swap places with any other willing rune-bearer within 15 feet. (The other rune-bearer can be bearing any rune.) Each creature must have room to appear in its new location or the effect is disrupted. This action has the concentrate and teleportation traits.

Invocation
(teleportation) The rune grows to an enormous size, swallowing up the rune-bearer and each Large or smaller creature adjacent to them, and then immediately spits them back out. Choose a square within a 15-foot emanation from the rune-bearer's original position for each swallowed creature to reappear. A Large creature doesn't necessarily need to reappear completely within the emanation, as long as one of its squares is. An unwilling creature avoids being teleported if it succeeds at a Will save against your class DC.

value.name: Trolistri, Rune of Forlorn Sorrow
value.description:
This rune calls to mind the beauty hidden in sorrow. While this rune is beautiful, sorrow is best admired from a distance, discouraging approach. Enemies within 20 feet of the rune-bearer treat all spaces between them and the rune-bearer as difficult terrain.

Invocation
Sorrow blots out the capacity for any other action. Each enemy in a 15-foot emanation around the rune-bearer must succeed at a Will saving throw or be slowed 1 for 1 round as it spends the first action of its next turn sobbing (slowed 2 on a critical failure). Regardless of the outcome, the creature is then temporarily immune to the invocation of trolistri, rune of forlorn sorrow for 1 hour.

value.name: Ulgatus, Rune of Restraint
value.description:
A faction of the constructed beings called automatons developed this rune to avoid the weaknesses of flesh. When the creature wearing the armor would gain or increase the value of their drained, enfeebled, or sickened condition, the rune attempts to prevent the imposition. The bearer attempts a DC 15 flat check. On a success, it doesn't gain or increase the value of that condition, but the rune goes temporarily dormant for 10 minutes. While dormant, the rune can't protect the bearer from conditions but can be invoked.

Invocation
The rune causes the armor to grow around the creature wearing it, fortifying any vulnerable spots. For 1 minute, the wearer gains resistance 10 to critical hits.

Level (17th) The DC of the flat check decreases to 10 and the resistance to critical hits increases to 20.

value.name: Yudici, Rune of Remonstrance
value.description:
This majestic rune grants the shield's wielder the conviction to aid their allies. While a shield bearing this rune is raised, its bearer emits an aura in a 10-foot emanation that grants their allies a +1 circumstance bonus to AC.

Invocation
The shield regains 40 Hit Points, and all of the bearer's allies in a 10-foot emanation gain a +1 status bonus to attack rolls and skill checks for 1 round.

Level (+3) The Hit Points restored increases by 10.

value.name: Eck-, Diacritic Rune of Phantasma
value.usage: drawn on a rune that deals damage
value.description:
This diacritic frames a base rune with almost invisible lines that turn the rune's effects against the bearer's soul. The damage dealt on the base rune becomes spirit damage, and each of your enemies adjacent to the rune-bearer takes 1d8 persistent spirit damage.

Level (17th) The persistent spirit damage increases by 1d8.

value.name: Inth-, Diacritic Rune of Corruption
value.description:
This set of angular accents around the base rune channels the essence of fiendish corruption. The base rune gains the unholy trait, as does any damage it deals. If applied to a holy creature, that creature is enfeebled 2 for as long as it bears the rune.

Invocation
(fire) When the base rune is invoked, it burns away in unholy black fire that lingers on its target. In addition to the base rune's normal effect, the target takes 2d4 persistent fire damage.

Level (+2) The persistent fire damage increases by 2d4.

value.name: Nesh-, Diacritic Rune of Contingency
value.description:
The wavy lines of this diacritic seem to stretch the base rune into a wider area. When you draw this rune, choose a trigger that when met will invoke the base rune, using the same restrictions as for the trigger of a Ready action. When the trigger is met, you can Invoke the base Rune as a reaction; you can't invoke any additional runes with that reaction. If you define complicated conditions, as determined by the GM, the trigger might fail.

You can have only one nesh-, diacritic rune of contingency applied at a given time, and once you invoke it, you can't etch or trace it again for 10 minutes.

value.name: Sar-, Diacritic Rune of Righteousness
value.description:
Clean arcs of gold faintly glow on the base rune, evoking celestial order and serenity. The base rune gains the holy trait, as does any damage it deals. If applied to an unholy creature, that creature is enfeebled 2 for as long as it bears the rune.

Invocation
When the base rune is invoked, it shines with holy light that harshly judges the target for any of its sins. In addition to the base rune's normal effect, the target is drained 1.

value.name: Aiuen, The Elf-Gate Key
value.description:
This masterful circular rune is a key to the aiudara network of elf gates that stretch across the stars. Once per turn, when the rune-bearer Strides, it can instead teleport a distance equal to its Speed.

Invocation
You teleport the rune-bearer to a location adjacent to any of your other runes, as long as it is on the same plane. An unwilling target can be teleported a maximum distance of 60 feet, and it avoids being teleported at all if it succeeds at a Will save against your class DC.

If you have the ability to cast the sigil cantrip, then you can use aiuen, the elf-gate key's invocation to teleport the rune-bearer to a location adjacent to any of your sigils on the same plane, in addition to any of your runes.

value.name: Ochygholl, The Poisoned Star
value.description:
This awe-inspiring rune of pointed curves is rumored to have been part of the magic that alghollthus used to call down the meteoroids of the Earthfall cataclysm. The rune-bearer senses a foreboding shadow overhead and that something terrible is about to happen. This dread is contagious. The rune-bearer becomes doomed 1, and its allies that begin their turn adjacent to the rune-bearer also become doomed 1 for 1 round. Each creature doomed this way takes 10 mental damage the first time each round it attempts an attack roll or skill check.

Invocation
(fire) The rune calls a meteorite down on the rune-bearer, fulfilling its terrible promise. Each creature in a 10-foot burst centered on a corner in the rune-bearer's space takes 3d10 bludgeoning damage with a basic Reflex save. Then, each creature within a 40-foot burst centered on that same corner takes 8d6 fire damage, also with a basic Reflex save. This invocation has the death trait for doomed creatures.

value.name: Rovan, Seal of the Dead Vault
value.description:
This mighty, jagged rune is just one of several that keeps the Destroyer sealed in his prison, deep in Golarion's core. The creature takes a –20-foot status penalty to its land Speed and a –40-foot status penalty to all other Speeds as the rune attempts to bind the creature. If a creature's fly Speed is reduced to 0 this way, it can't take the Fly or Arrest a Fall actions.

Invocation
(incapacitation) The ground in the rune-bearer's space and in a 10-foot emanation becomes difficult terrain permanently, and the rune-bearer must attempt a Fortitude saving throw as the earth around it attempts to surround and imprison it. The rune-bearer is then immune to your rovan, seal of the Dead Vault runes for 24 hours.

Critical Success The bearer is unaffected.

Success The rune-bearer becomes slowed 1 for 1 round.

Failure The rune-bearer becomes slowed 2 for 1 round.

Critical Failure The bearer becomes restrained and blinded as it is trapped in a massive, compressed sphere of earth. While restrained, the bearer is also slowed 2. If the bearer is unable to escape the sphere within 3 rounds, it becomes petrified. Over the course of a year, the sphere forms a small hill around it, hiding its buried prisoner. At the top of the hill, a stone with the image of this rune remains. Counteracting the stone frees the prisoner.

value.name: Xinsala, The Well of Virtues
value.description:
This complex rune comprises many different ligatures from the ancient Thassilonian runes representing the seven virtues of rule, before they were corrupted by the runelords. When drawn, it creates a well of glowing energy that occupies the square it's drawn on and creates an aura of swirling, virtuous runes in a 30-foot emanation. While in the aura, you or any of your allies gain a +1 status bonus to AC against magic, a +1 status bonus to saving throws against magic, and resistance 10 to damage from magical effects.

Invocation
(healing, vitality) The well explodes outward with invigorating force. The well heals any number of creatures in its area for a total of 70 Hit Points divided as you choose, and you and each of your allies in the area gain a +20-foot status bonus to your Speeds and are quickened for 1 round. The extra action from quickened can be used only to Stride or Strike.

value.name: Absorb Magic
value.trigger: Another creature within 30 feet Casts a Spell or uses an action, activity, or reaction with the arcane, divine, magical, occult, or primal trait.
value.description: You breathe in a small fraction of the magic produced by the triggering effect, storing it in your internal nexus. You become overflowing. You remain overflowing for up to 1 minute before the stored magical energy fades. While overflowing, you gain a +1 status bonus to saving throws against effects with the arcane, divine, magical, occult, and primal traits. This bonus becomes +2 at 15th level.

value.name: Overflowing Blade
value.description: You conduct the magic in your internal nexus to coat your weapon or unarmed strike, empowering it with magical energy for a devastating attack. Make a melee Strike. If the Strike hits, you deal an additional 1d4 force damage. At 10th level, the additional damage increases to 2d4 force damage. At 18th level, the additional damage increases to 3d4 force damage. You are no longer overflowing.

value.name: Rouse the World
value.description: The flora, fauna, and elements in a 10-foot burst within 30 feet stir, aiding you and your allies and whispering in your ear. This area is known as your waking world. While in your waking world, you and your allies gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Athletics and Acrobatics checks, and you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Nature checks to Recall Knowledge about creatures and hazards in the area. The effect lasts for 10 minutes, but you can Dismiss it. Once per round on subsequent turns, you can Sustain this ability to increase the burst’s size by 10 feet. You can Rouse the World in only one area at a time; if you use this ability again, the first area returns to normal.

value.name: Draconic Gift
value.description: A palm-sized magic item — its appearance chosen when you take Draconic Acolyte Dedication — with a level equal to your level and a trait matching your draconic benefactor's tradition. It is linked to your spirit: if you ever lose possession of it (whether by dropping it or having it stolen from your person), it appears back in your possession at the beginning of your next turn.

value.note: As described in the champion class. Your deity's Sanctification entry decides which of these you may take.

value.name: Transformation Seal
value.description: A mundane-seeming item of light Bulk — a ring, brooch, or key — that has the arcane trait, given to you by one of the constellations of the Tian Xia zodiac. If your seal is ever lost or destroyed, you can gain a replacement by spending 1 week of downtime in introspection to reconnect with your constellation. You, and only you, can transform into your sentinel form by Activating the seal.

value.name: Mind Weapon
value.description: A melee weapon you imagine into the material world. It is a martial melee weapon with one of four basic statistics chosen when you gain it: one-handed 1d4 (agile, finesse); one-handed 1d6 (finesse); one-handed 1d8; or two-handed 1d10 (reach). Each day during your daily preparations you decide whether it deals bludgeoning damage and is in the club group, piercing damage and the spear group, or slashing damage and the sword group. Your mind weapon is an extension of your mind — it has no Hardness, and any ability that would damage it instead damages you directly as mental damage of the same amount.

value.name: Mind Smith's Keepsake
value.description: An object of light Bulk — a bracelet, a figurine — that you wear or keep on your person and inscribe with weapon runes. The runes you etch into your keepsake apply to your mind weapon.

value.name: Command a Thrall
value.description: You make one of your thralls Crawl, Drop Prone, Escape, Interact, Stand, Stride, or Strike. A thrall can take only simple Interact actions, not ones that require skill checks or complicated movements. However, they can make checks to Escape using your spell attack modifier; escaping this way uses and counts toward your multiple attack penalty. When you Command a Thrall to Strike, it makes a melee unarmed Strike using your spell attack modifier, dealing 1d6 bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage; at 5th level and every 4 levels thereafter the damage increases by 1d6.

value:
You put your alchemical interest into practice. You become trained in alchemical bombs, the alchemist class DC, and Crafting; if you were already trained in Crafting, you instead become trained in a skill of your choice.

You gain the Quick Alchemy benefits, creating up to 4 versatile vials during your daily preparations. Add the formulas for four additional common alchemical items to your formula book, in addition to those you gain from Alchemical Crafting.

value.name: Part the Veil
value.description:
**Requirements** You are not observed by any enemies.

---

You phase yourself into the interstices, veiling yourself from physical reality. You become concealed. You can use this concealment to Hide or Sneak as your disassociation from reality makes you difficult to focus on. If you use a hostile action, this effect ends after the action is complete; otherwise, it lasts for 1 minute.

value.name: Solitary Invocation
value.description: You utter the name of one of your runes within 30 feet, which blazes with power, applying the effect in its Invocation entry. An invoked rune then fades away, its task complete.

value.name: Palatine Detective's Charm
value.description: A small charm you crafted from your study of the occult and divine, usually taking the form of a silver chain, a golden scarab, or a withered hand. While you wear this charm, you gain a +1 status bonus to saving throws against mental effects, and you can brandish it to use Mystic Aegis.

value: You’re able to shift yourself into the spaces between to avoid notice. You gain the Part the Veil action.

You become trained in runesmith class DC and Crafting. You gain a runic repertoire with two 1st-level runes of your choice. You choose these from the common runes on the rune list as well as uncommon or rarer runes you have access to.

You can etch runes. An etched rune is carved, inked, or branded; this application does not damage the creature or item. Etching a rune requires an artisan's toolkit. Your magic can sustain up to one etched rune at a time. If you're at least 9th level, increase the maximum number of etched runes you can sustain at a time to 2, and if you're at least 17th level, increase it to 3. You can etch any number of runes up to your maximum during your daily preparations or by spending 10 minutes in exploration mode. Your etched runes remain indefinitely until they're expended or removed or until you etch more runes than your maximum, which causes your oldest rune to fade. Additionally, you gain the Solitary Invocation action.

options.label: Aquatic
options.description: If you have unimpeded journey: you gain a swim Speed equal to your Speed. If you already had a swim Speed, you instead gain a +10-foot status bonus to your swim Speed.

options.label: Arctic
options.description: If you have unimpeded journey: you need to eat and drink only one-tenth as much as usual, you aren't affected by severe or extreme cold, and you can walk across ice and snow at full Speed without needing to Balance.

options.label: Desert

options.label: Plains

options.label: Sky

options.label: Swamp

options.label: Underground

The second benefit above arrives only with the unimpeded journey class feature (ranger 11th) and only while you are actually in that terrain, so it is carried as a conditional star on Speed rather than folded into the number. Terrain Master lets you spend 1 hour practicing in your current terrain to make it your favored terrain temporarily.
